kentucky.name: Kentucky
kentucky.summary: The heartland of American whiskey: sweet corn, charred new oak and rickhouse heat cycling.

bourbon.serve: Neat, on the rocks, or in an Old Fashioned
bourbon.expect: Sweet, full and oaky: caramel corn and vanilla with charred-oak spice.

style.label: Straight bourbon · Sweet corn & charred oak
style.method: At least 51% corn mashbill, charred new American oak barrels
style.effect: New charred oak gives bourbon its caramel-vanilla signature in a few hot-warehouse years

bottles.name: Elijah Craig Small Batch
bottles.note: Spearmint, caramel and baking spice at 94 proof

bottles.name: Wild Turkey 101
bottles.note: High-proof, punchy and classic

bottles.name: Four Roses Single Barrel
bottles.note: Floral and fruity from unique yeast strains

bourbon.dilution: Bottled in Bond (100 proof) expressions take a cube well; 90–95 proof is fine either way
bourbon.ice: Excellent on rocks and in cocktails — the classic bourbon serves

wheated-bourbon.expect: Soft, round and dessert-like: wheated mashbills trade rye spice for gentle sweetness.

style.label: Wheated bourbon · Soft & rounded
style.method: Corn plus wheat instead of rye in the mashbill, charred new oak
style.effect: Wheat removes rye's bite, giving a smoother, sweeter pour

bottles.name: Maker's Mark
bottles.note: The accessible wheated benchmark with its red-dipped neck

bottles.name: W.L. Weller 12
bottles.note: Cult wheater with dusty oak and caramel

wheated-bourbon.dilution: Maker's Mark (45%) needs no water; Weller 12 too
wheated-bourbon.ice: Excellent over ice; the soft wheat profile suits a cube

rye.expect: Dry and assertively spicy: rye's herbal kick over oak sweetness.

style.label: Straight rye · Spicy & dry
style.method: At least 51% rye mashbill, charred new oak
style.effect: Rye grain contributes herbal, peppery spice distinct from corn sweetness

bottles.name: Rittenhouse Rye Bottled in Bond
bottles.note: 100-proof rye staple for Manhattans

bottles.name: Bulleit Rye
bottles.note: Kentucky-bottled but distilled at MGP in Indiana from a 95% rye mashbill: dry and herbal

rye.dilution: Rittenhouse (100 proof) takes ice or water well
rye.ice: Good on rocks; best in stirred cocktails

identity.setting: Limestone plateau with hot summers and cold winters
identity.terrain: Rolling bluegrass plains and river valleys
identity.soil: Limestone-filtered spring water, low in iron
influences: Rickhouse temperature cycling drives fast extraction
Limestone water ideal for sour mash

why.cause: Hot summers and cold winters in the rickhouse
why.effect: Barrels breathe deeply, extracting oak quickly — bourbon matures in years, not decades
The char strips harsh sulfur notes; beneath it, the heat-caramelised 'red layer' of wood sugars gives vanilla and caramel

why.cause: Limestone spring water, low in iron and carrying calcium and magnesium
why.effect: Supports healthy sour-mash fermentation; iron would darken and spoil the spirit

tennessee.name: Tennessee
tennessee.summary: Bourbon's charcoal-mellowed cousin: filtered through sugar maple before aging for extra smoothness.

tennessee.serve: Neat, on the rocks, or with cola
tennessee.expect: Smooth and charcoal-softened: corn sweetness, banana and caramel with a dry, sooty-char edge.

style.label: Tennessee whiskey · Charcoal-mellowed
style.method: Bourbon-style mashbill filtered through sugar-maple charcoal (Lincoln County Process) before barreling
style.effect: Charcoal mellowing removes sharp congeners before the barrel; it filters the spirit rather than adding smoke

bottles.name: Jack Daniel's Old No. 7
bottles.note: The global face of Tennessee whiskey

bottles.name: George Dickel No. 12
bottles.note: Smoother, slightly sweeter rival from Cascade Hollow

tennessee.ice: Classic with ice; charcoal mellowness survives mixers

influences: Lincoln County Process legally required for 'Tennessee whiskey'
Spring water sources, most famously Jack Daniel's Cave Spring Hollow

why.cause: Dripping through feet of sugar-maple charcoal before aging
why.effect: Strips harsh grain edges early, making the whiskey taste older than its age

why.cause: Same charred new-oak barrels as bourbon
why.effect: Keeps caramel and vanilla in common with its Kentucky cousin

ireland.name: Ireland
ireland.summary: Smooth, unpeated and often triple-distilled: the world's lightest and most approachable whiskey tradition.

pot-still.serve: Neat or with a single ice cube
pot-still.expect: Silky and spice-creamy with barley sweetness: Ireland's signature pot still character.

style.label: Single pot still · Creamy & spicy
style.method: Mash of malted and unmalted barley, triple distilled in pot stills
style.effect: Unmalted barley gives a distinctive oily, spicy 'pot still character'

bottles.name: Redbreast 12
bottles.note: The definitive pot still whiskey: sherry, spice and cream

bottles.name: Green Spot
bottles.note: Single pot still made by Midleton for the Dublin wine merchants Mitchell & Son: fruity and rounded

pot-still.dilution: 40–46%; Redbreast's cask-strength editions take water well
pot-still.ice: A cube is a common Irish serve; purists prefer neat or with water

blended-irish.serve: On the rocks, in coffee, or as a highball
blended-irish.expect: Light, smooth and easygoing: grain lightness plus pot still character.

style.label: Blended Irish · Light & smooth
style.method: Column-still grain whiskey blended with triple-distilled pot still whiskey
style.effect: Grain lightness plus pot still texture and spice gives the famously smooth Irish profile

bottles.name: Jameson
bottles.note: The global standard Irish blend

bottles.name: Bushmills Black Bush
bottles.note: Malt-led exception: mostly triple-distilled malt with a grain component, sherried

why.effect: A third pass removes more heavy compounds, giving the famous smoothness

why.cause: Pot still whiskey as the flavour component
why.effect: Unmalted barley adds the creamy, lightly spicy texture in the blend's core

blended-irish.ice: Built for ice and mixers; its light body is mixer-friendly

irish-malt.serve: Neat or with a single ice cube
irish-malt.expect: Triple-distilled malt: lighter and fruitier than Scottish malts, with no smoke.

style.label: Irish single malt · Light & fruity
style.method: Triple-distilled pot-still malted barley, ex-bourbon and sherry casks
style.effect: Triple distillation gives Irish malt its lighter, cleaner character

bottles.name: Bushmills 10
bottles.note: Triple-distilled single malt: honeyed, light and fruity

irish-malt.ice: A cube suits the light triple-distilled style

influences: Aeneas Coffey's column still (1830) was an Irish invention, though Irish distillers largely shunned it at first
Unmalted barley tradition from tax-avoidance history

why.effect: A third pass removes more heavy compounds, giving the famous smoothness
Historically no smoke — Ireland's clean, bright style

why.cause: Unmalted barley in pot still whiskey
why.effect: Adds a creamy, peppery texture no other country replicates

japan.name: Japan
japan.climate: Four distinct seasons; cold winters, humid summers
japan.summary: Malt whisky built on Scottish methods with local precision; styles range from unpeated fruit-forward flagships to clean, lightly peated forest expressions.

japanese-malt-unpeated.serve: Neat, with a few drops of water, or on the rocks
japanese-malt-unpeated.dilution: Typically 43% ABV; a few drops of water soften the heat. Mizuwari (roughly one part whisky to two parts water) is a traditional way to open aromatics
japanese-malt-unpeated.ice: Suntory recommends its malt whiskies on the rocks and in highballs as well as neat — follow the expression and your own taste
japanese-malt-unpeated.ageing: 12-year flagships are the classic reference points; no-age-statement editions vary more batch to batch
japanese-malt-unpeated.expect: Refined and fruity: orchard and stone fruit over delicate oak, with no peat smoke.

style.label: Japanese unpeated malt · Refined & fruity
style.method: Scottish-style pot distillation; mizunara oak appears mainly in long-matured or premium editions (Suntory)
style.effect: Mizunara is a leak-prone, slow-growing oak historically used when imported casks were scarce; coopered carefully, it contributes sandalwood and incense-like aromas (Suntory)

bottles.name: Yamazaki 12
bottles.note: Unpeated flagship: fruit, subtle oak spice and balance (Suntory)

japanese-malt-peated.phenol: lightly peated — the Hakushu house style
japanese-malt-peated.serve: Neat, with a few drops of water, or on the rocks
japanese-malt-peated.dilution: Typically 43% ABV; a few drops of water soften the heat
japanese-malt-peated.ice: Suntory explicitly recommends Hakushu on the rocks and in highballs (Suntory's Hakushu serving suggestions)
japanese-malt-peated.expect: Forest freshness with gentle, clean peat: pine and mint over soft smoke.

style.label: Japanese lightly peated malt · Forest & mint
style.method: Lightly peated barley, pot distillation (Suntory's Hakushu)
style.effect: Hakushu's light peating reads clean and green rather than medicinal

bottles.name: Hakushu 12
bottles.note: Lightly peated: pine, mint and clean gentle smoke (Suntory)

japanese-highball-blend.serve: As a highball (whisky and soda over ice), mizuwari, or on the rocks
japanese-highball-blend.ageing: Blends of various ages; core ranges carry no age statement
japanese-highball-blend.expect: Light, crisp and citrusy: built for the highball glass rather than neat tasting.

style.label: Japanese highball blend · Light & crisp
style.method: Malt and grain whiskies blended deliberately light for highball service (Suntory Toki)
style.effect: Blended to stay coherent when stretched with soda — the signature serve of this branch of Japanese whisky

bottles.name: Suntory Toki
bottles.note: Built for the highball boom: light, crisp, citrusy

japanese-highball-blend.dilution: Core-range blends are typically 40–43% and blended to stay balanced when stretched; mizuwari uses roughly one part whisky to two parts water
japanese-highball-blend.ice: The highball is the signature serve for this style in Japan; Suntory recommends its blends for highballs

japan-made-bold-blend.serve: Neat, with a splash of water, as a highball, or on the rocks
japan-made-bold-blend.dilution: Bottled at 51.4% ABV; a splash of water opens the aromatics and softens the heat
japan-made-bold-blend.ice: A large cube is workable; many drinkers prefer water to keep the dense flavor intact
japan-made-bold-blend.ageing: Married from malt and grain components — including selected imported whisky — at higher strength (Nikka's From the Barrel)
japan-made-bold-blend.expect: Bold and full-bodied: dense oak and dried fruit with a warming, higher-strength finish. Includes selected imported whisky (Nikka).

style.label: Japan-made bold blend · Full & robust
style.method: Malt-forward blend bottled at high strength after marrying; includes selected imported whisky alongside Japanese components (Nikka)
style.effect: Its high strength and concentration keep the flavour dense even when diluted with water or soda (Nikka)

bottles.name: Nikka From the Barrel
bottles.note: Malt-forward blend at 51.4% ABV; includes selected imported whisky; bold, dense and full-bodied (Nikka)

identity.terrain: Varied: Yamazaki near Kyoto, Hakushu in mountain forest, Yoichi on Hokkaido's coast
influences: Yamazaki (1923) and Yoichi (1934) founded the tradition
Mizunara oak used mainly in long-matured or premium editions

why.cause: Founders Masataka Taketsuru and Shinjiro Torii trained in or drew directly on Scotch methods
why.effect: Japanese malt whisky follows Scottish-style pot distillation with local precision (Suntory, Nikka company histories)

why.cause: Mizunara oak is leak-prone and difficult to cooper, and was originally used out of necessity when imported barrels were scarce
why.effect: Its distinctive sandalwood and incense notes became a prized signature mainly in long-matured expressions (Suntory)
Blends are engineered to stay balanced when diluted; this is a stylistic choice, not a quality hierarchy

canada.name: Canada
canada.summary: Light, smooth and rye-inflected: a blending tradition built for easy drinking.

canadian-blended.serve: On the rocks or in cocktails
canadian-blended.ageing: Legal minimum 3 years; core blends often carry 6 years or more
canadian-blended.expect: Light and gentle with a rye whisper: cocktail-friendly and easy-sipping.

style.label: Canadian blended · Light & rye-soft
style.method: Column-still base whiskies blended with a small 'flavouring whisky' often rye-heavy
style.effect: Blending a light base with a flavourful rye component gives smoothness plus subtle spice

bottles.name: Crown Royal
bottles.note: The Canadian standard: smooth, caramel-soft

bottles.name: Lot No. 40
bottles.note: Not a blend: 100% rye from a copper pot still — the rye lover's Canadian

canadian-blended.dilution: 40% standard; designed to be served without added water
canadian-blended.ice: Ice-friendly by design; the classic Canadian serve for this style

identity.soil: Rich prairie soils growing rye and corn
influences: Historically 'rye' means Canadian whisky, even with small rye content

why.cause: Grains are usually distilled and aged separately, then blended after maturation
why.effect: A light corn base plus a smaller, flavourful rye component gives smoothness with subtle spice
Slower oak extraction keeps the palate light
